intro: A percentile is ambiguous until its interpolation convention is fixed. Build quantiles from sorted observations and fractional positions.
task: Return a vector of empirical quantiles using position h=(n-1)*q and linear interpolation between neighboring sorted observations.
requirements: values is a nonempty vector. probabilities is a vector with every entry in [0,1]; its order need not be sorted.
For each q, set h=(n-1)*q, lo=floor(h), hi=ceil(h), and interpolate sorted[lo]*(1-fraction)+sorted[hi]*fraction.
Preserve the query order and repeated queries. A single observation produces that value for every q.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Sort the observations once, then map each query to a fractional index between the first and last observation.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Floor and ceiling locate the two neighbors; the fractional index supplies the interpolation weight.

explanation: Quantile conventions choose where sorted observations sit on the probability axis. This exercise places the first and last observations at zero and one, then interpolates between them.
A median for an even-sized sample therefore averages the two central observations. Query order is independent of observation sorting and should remain unchanged.
